heading: Roles decide the folder, modifiers do not
body:
A MoneyService with Service belongs in services/MoneyService.<ext>. RequestRoute (a controller), Service, Store, HTTPClient (a client), Helper, Converter, Setup and Entity each require their standard suffix. They also require their lowercase plural role folder: controllers, services, stores, remotes (the old name clients still works), helpers, converters, setups and entities. The file may sit in a nested folder inside it, such as services/billing/InvoiceService.ts. A nested folder adds no new injection name, so two variants of the same service in one language are still an error. `ty migrate fix --write` moves the files of an old clients/ folder to remotes/ and changes the imports that it recognizes; it refuses to overwrite a file that already exists in remotes/ (ADR 0088). Abstract classes, interfaces, protocols, traits, type aliases and files that only re-export are not roles, so they need no marker. A folder does not register a class: a class in a role folder without its marker fails with TY1363 (ADR 0091). An IdentityProvider class also lives in controllers and ends with IdentityProvider. A role type for Allow is an empty class in server/roles, named after the role, such as server/roles/Admin.ts. The type name needs a domain prefix (a word for its subject, such as Money). The filename stem (the name without the extension) must match the type name with exact case. An annotated source file contains exactly one class and its imports. A worker and the project-root middleware follow the same rule, even without a framework marker. For a Rust impl, the compiler checks its target type. For a Go method, it checks the receiver type. Conflicting primary roles fail, so split the types into separate files. No second top-level class, function, interface, type alias, enum, constant, variable or statement is allowed. Pure data types belong in models/. Plain helper code becomes a static method of a utility class in client/shared/utils or server/utils (a class whose name ends with Utils, with no annotation), or a method on the class that owns it. Annotated helper types need their own file. When the helper is a managed provider, use a role file such as helpers/PriceHelper.ts with Helper. Settings and validation data, such as OrderInput with Checked or Endpoint with Setting, are models: they live in models/ without a role (ADR 0092). So Tachyon does not treat their validation and configuration fields as injected dependencies. The compiler adds their behavior metadata. But it does not register them for dependency injection. In dependency injection, Tachyon creates the objects a class needs and gives them to it. Tachyon does not discover files with no framework annotations as providers. A Rust struct and all impl blocks for that same type form one class. A Go type and the methods on it also form one class. In other languages, nested types stay inside their owner. Violations fail with TY1310 before the compiler composes (joins) the generated units. The compiler joins separately checked files that you write into a generated program. That generated program may contain several behavior types. Modifiers such as Needs, Named, Table, WhenProfile, Settings, Checked and Setting do not add suffix or folder requirements. Both realms share every role except the controllers: RequestRoute and SocketRoute classes exist only in Yon (ADR 0048). StreamRoute is a method marker inside a controller, not a role. A Tac service is client/services/<Name>Service, and a view addresses it as {name.field}. A Yon service is server/services/<Name>Service, and Tachyon injects it into a controller. A Yon controller is server/controllers/<Name>Controller, and its annotations declare its URLs. These are strict Tachyon conventions. Spring Boot does not require them.

`server/gateways/` is reserved. Tachyon writes the generated units of `@Gateway` class targets there, inside its own snapshot. A file that you write in that folder fails with `TY1310`.

This rule does not add a module linker (a tool that connects separate modules). A Yon role file that the compiler includes, such as a service, may not use a relative import or `require` (`TY2101`). Use the standard-library and realm-root import forms, such as `/models/Guide.ts`, or no import at all: role classes of the same realm and language find each other by name. A Tac JavaScript or TypeScript file may import a file of its own realm with a relative path. No file imports a file of the other realm (`TY1369`). A worker Handler can keep its supported ordinary imports.
